Rashi on Nedarim 48a:1:1.english: From an object of that city - For they belong to both of them.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:1:2.english: And the cistern in the middle - As [the Gemara] explains at the end of the last chapter of Eruvin (daf 104a).

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:1:3.english: And the scrolls - Torah scrolls toward which both of them contributed money with the residents of that city.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:1:4.english: And one who writes his portion to the Nasi - In the Gemara it explains it.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:2:1.hebrew: שהכותב לנשיא א"צ לזכות - ע"י אחר, אבל הכותב להדיוט צריך לזכות. ובזה כח נשיא יפה מכח הדיוט:
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:2:1.english: That one who writes [his portion] to the Nasi need not confer possession - through another [person], whereas one who writes [it] to a common person must confer possession [through another]. And in this [respect], the power of a Nasi is greater than the power of a common person.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:2:2.english: In the prevalent [case] - For such is the custom, to show honor to the Nasi.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:5:1.english: It is taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi Yehuda says: The people of Galilee are quarrelsome - They are short-tempered.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:5:2.hebrew: וכתבו - מדבר של אותה העיר לנשיא, כוי שיהו אלו ואלו מותרין בהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:5:2.english: And they wrote - [from] the property of that city to the Nasi, so that both these and those would be permitted [to benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:6:1.hebrew: המודר הנאה מחבירו ואין לו מה יאכל - הך מתניתין אייתי נמי לעיל באידך פירקין (נדרים ד' מג.), אלא דהתם לא נקט לה אלא משום דיוקא, משום דבעי למיתנא עלה הפקר דפליג בה רבי יוסי:
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:6:1.english: One who is prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit from another and he does not have anything to eat - This Mishnah was also brought above in the other chapter (Nedarim 43a), except that there [the Tanna] only cited it for the sake of the inference, because he wanted to teach regarding it [the law of] ownerless property, about which Rabbi Yosei disagrees.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:7:1.english: And the sin will be hung on his head - That his father, who is prohibited by vow [from deriving] benefit, will eat through him [the recipient].

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:7:2.hebrew: אמרו חכמים כל מתנה שאינה - כל כך ברשות המקבל, שאם הקדישה אינה מקודשת, אינה מתנה:
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:7:2.english: The Sages said: Any gift that is not - to such an extent in the possession of the recipient that if he consecrated it, it is not consecrated, is not a gift.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:8:1.hebrew: מעשה לסתור - דברישא קתני המודר הנאה וכו', וקתני תקנתא דמצי למעבד כה"ג, והדר תני נעשה וכו' לסתור דבריו הראשונים:
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:8:1.english: [Was] an incident [cited] to contradict - For in the first clause [the Mishnah] teaches, "One who is prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit, etc.," and teaches a remedy that one may act in this manner; and then it teaches, "It happened [i.e., an incident occurred], etc.," to contradict its first words.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:8:2.english: [The Mishnah] is incomplete and this is what it teaches - In our Mishnah: "One who is prohibited by a vow from [deriving] benefit," etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:8:3.hebrew: ואם הוכיח סופו על תחלתו - שלא נתן לו אלא על מנת שיתן לזה ייאכל, אסור. ומעשה נמי וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:8:3.english: And if his ultimate [action] proved [his] initial [intent] - [meaning] that he gave [it] to him only on condition that he give [it] to this [other person] so that he eat [it], [it is] forbidden. And [there was] also an incident, etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:9:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דאינה מתנה, אלא דאמר ליה והינן לפניך, דמשמע דהכי א"ל: והינן נתונין לך אלא על מנת שיבא אבא:
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:9:1.english: They taught [this] only - that it is not a gift, except where he said to him, "And they are before you [only...]," which implies that this is what he said to him: "And they are given to you only on condition that my father comes."

Rashi on Nedarim 48a:9:2.hebrew: אבל אמר ליה והן לפניך שיבא אבא ויאכל מדיעתיה הוא דקא אמר ליה - דהכי משמע: "והן נתונים לך והם בדעתך", שיבא אבא הוי דוקא לו: ע"א: אמר רבא: לא תידוק ותימא דאיכא חילוק בין "והינן לפניך" בין "והן לפניך", דודאי תרוייהו אסירי, דהא סעודתו מוכחת עליו שלא נתן לו אלא על מנת שיבוא אביו ויאכל, דה"ל כמ"ד "והינן לפניך":
Rashi on Nedarim 48a:9:2.english: But [if] he said to him: "And they are before you, that [my] father may come and eat," he is saying to him [that it is] at his discretion - For this is what it implies: "And they are given to you, and they are at your discretion"; [whether my] father comes is solely up to him. Another explanation: Rava said: Do not infer and say that there is a distinction between "and they are before you" (vehinan lefanecha) and "and they are before you" (vehen lefanecha), for certainly both of them are prohibited, since his meal proves about him that he gave [it] to him only on condition that his father come and eat, so that it is like one who says "and they are before you" (vehinan lefanecha).

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:10:1.hebrew: סעודתו מוכיח עליו - שלא היה בדעתו ליתן כ"א שיבא אביו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:10:1.english: His meal proves about him - that he did not intend to give [the gift] except [so] that his father would come.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:1.hebrew: בדברים של אותה העיר - שהם דרים בה, שהן (מפני) שותפין, וזה אסור מפני חלקו של זה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:1.english: From objects of that city - [the city] in which they dwell, for they are partners, and this one is prohibited [from benefiting] because of the portion of that one.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:2.hebrew: רחבה ומרחץ ובית הכנסת - אתיא כרבנן דאסרו בחצר, דאין ברירה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:2.english: The square, and the bathhouse, and the synagogue - [This] accords with the Rabbis who prohibited [entering] a courtyard, because there is no retroactive designation (bereirah).

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:3.hebrew: אסור ברחבה ובבית הכנסת - יש לדקדק: לכאורה משמע דאתי' כרבנן דאמרי אין ברירה, ולא אמר "האי בדידיה קמהלך" כמו בחצר לרבי אליעזר. ובפרק בתרא דביצה (דף לט -) גבי בור דמתניתין דעולי בבל, קבעי למימר דמתני' דהכא אית ליה ברירה, ולכך מותר בבור, משום דהאי בדידיה קממלא והאי בדידיה קממלא. ואם כן, אמאי אסור בבית הכנסת ובדברים של אותה העיר? ויש לחלק: [בממלא] מים מן הבור — בהא סבר תנא דיש ברירה, בהא שהוא מסלקו מחלק חבירו; אבל להשתמש או להכנס בדבר שחבירו שותף — ודאי לית להו ברירה. וה"ה דהוי מצי למיתני דשניהן מותרין למלאות מבור שבעיר, בפרק הדר (עירובין מה:). עוד נראה להר"ר שמואל מאויר"א ז"ל דסוגיא דהתם סברה כסברא דריש פירקין, דרבנן סברי שפיר דיש ברירה, ולא אסרו אלא (בברירה) משום קנסא; ודווקא בדברים של אותה העיר, אבל בדברים של עולי בבל לא רצו לקנוס, לפי שהוא לכל העולם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:3.english: [He is] prohibited in the square and in the synagogue - One must examine [this] closely: seemingly it implies that [our Mishnah] follows the Rabbis who say there is no bereirah [retroactive designation], and [it] does not say "this one walks in his own [portion]" as [is said] regarding a courtyard according to Rabbi Eliezer. Yet in the last chapter of Beitzah (39), regarding the cistern of our Mishnah belonging to those who ascended from Babylonia, [the Gemara] seeks to say that our Mishnah here holds that there is bereirah, and therefore it is permitted [to draw] from the cistern, because this one draws from his own [water] and that one draws from his own [water]. And if so, why is it prohibited in the synagogue and with objects of that city? And one can distinguish: [when one draws] water from the cistern — in that case the Tanna holds there is bereirah, insofar as he removes himself from his fellow's share; however, to use or to enter something in which his fellow is a partner — certainly they do not hold [that there is] bereirah. And the same applies that [the Mishnah] could have taught that both of them are permitted to draw from a cistern in the city, [as discussed] in the chapter [entitled] Hadar (Eruvin 45b). Furthermore, it appears to Rabbi Shmuel of Évreux, of blessed memory, that the sugya there holds like the opinion at the beginning of our chapter, that the Rabbis indeed hold there is bereirah, and they only prohibited [it] (with bereirah) because of a penalty; and specifically regarding objects of that city, whereas regarding objects of those who ascended from Babylonia they did not wish to penalize, since it is for the entire world.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:4.hebrew: והתיבה - ארון שנותנין בו ס"ת:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:4.english: And the ark - A chest in which they place a Torah scroll.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:5.english: And the books - They were accustomed to buy books with public [funds] for the residents of the city to study from them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:6.hebrew: והכותב חלקו לנשיא - מפרש בגמרא דה"ק: כיצד תקנתם? יכתבו חלקם לנשיא. והא דלעיל גבי חצר לא קאמר הך תקנתא — דחצר, שהיא מיוחדת ממש, אין תקנה לתת אותה לנשיא. אבל הכא, דמעיקרא נמי אין כל הדברים הללו מיוחדים להם, לא יפסידו אם יכתבו חלקם לנשיא, שגם אחר כך יכולין לילך וליהנות, שהנשיא לא יקפיד עליהן, כיון שגם לו אינה מיוחדת שהרי היא לכל בני העיר. ולנשיא לאו דווקא, ה"ה אם לאחד מבני העיר, אלא לרווחא דמילתא נקט, כדמוכח לקמן: "לא דברו חכמים אלא בהווה". והטעם — לפי שחולקים כבוד לנשיא. א"נ, כיון שאנו מתחילים לעשות תקנה בחלק זה, יש לנו לעשות התקנה הטובה שנוכל; ואם נתקן שיתנוהו לאחד מבני העיר, שגם הוא ידיר אחד מחבירו הנאה, אבל הנשיא אינו רגיל להדיר ולהקפיד על ישראל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:1:6.english: And one who writes his portion [over] to the Nasi - The Gemara explains that this is what [the Mishnah] means: What is their remedy? They should write [over] their portion to the Nasi. And [as for] why [the Mishnah] did not state this remedy earlier regarding a courtyard — because [for] a courtyard, which is truly designated [for their private use], there is no remedy to give it to the Nasi. However, here, where from the outset as well none of these things are designated [exclusively] for them, they will not lose out if they write [over] their portion to the Nasi, since even afterward they can go and derive benefit [from them], for the Nasi will not object to them, since it is not designated for him either, as it belongs to all the residents of the city. And "to the Nasi" is not meant literally [as exclusive] — the same applies if [one writes it over] to one of the residents of the city — rather, [the Mishnah] stated [this] as a matter of common practice, as is proven below: "The Sages spoke only of the common case." And the reason [they specifically mentioned the Nasi] is because they accord honor to the Nasi. Alternatively, since we are beginning to institute a remedy in this matter, we should institute the best remedy that we can; and if we were to institute that they give it to one of the residents of the city, [there is a concern] that he too might prohibit his fellow from deriving benefit [from him] by a vow, whereas the Nasi is not accustomed to prohibit [people] by a vow or to be particular against Israel:

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:2:1.hebrew: אין צריך לקנות - דאלים כחו, ולכך תיקנו שיכתוב לנשיא דאין צריך לקנות; שאם יתקנו לכתוב לאחר, פעמים ישכחו לזכות ואתי לידי תקלה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:2:1.english: There is no need to acquire [it] - Because his [the Nasi's] power is strong, and therefore they instituted that one should write [one's share] to the Nasi, as there is no need to acquire [it]; for if they were to institute writing [it] to another [person], at times they would forget to confer possession, and it would lead to a stumbling block.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:2:2.hebrew: שכבר כתבו אביהם - כלומר, זכותם כתבו לנשיא מדורות הראשונים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:2:2.english: For their fathers already wrote [it] - That is to say, they wrote their rights [over] to the Nasi from the earlier generations.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:3:1.english: Why is it forbidden - because he wrote his portion [over] to the Nasi?

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:5:1.hebrew: עמדו אבותיהם - ראשי בית אבות שלהם, והכריחום שיכתבו חלקיהם לנשיא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:5:1.english: Their forefathers arose - [This refers to] the heads of their ancestral houses, and they compelled them to write their portions [over] to the Nasi.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:7:1.hebrew: כל מתנה שאם הקדישה אינה מקודשת אינה מתנה - כלומר, שאם הקדישה בעודה בידו אינה מקודשת — אינה מתנה גם לשאר מינים, ואסור אביו ליכנס בחצר. וא"ת: והא אמר מתנה על מנת להחזיר שמה מתנה? וי"ל: דהתם, כל כמה דלא החזיר הוי מתנה גמורה לכל מה שירצה; אבל הכא אין בידו להקנותה לשום אדם, דלא נתנה אלא כדי שיאכל אביו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:7:1.english: Any gift that, if he consecrated it, is not consecrated, is not a gift - That is to say, if he consecrated it while it was in his possession [and] it is not consecrated, it is not a gift even for other matters, and his father is forbidden to enter the courtyard. And if you ask: But did [the Gemara] not say [that] a gift [given] on condition to be returned is considered a gift? And one can answer: There, as long as he has not returned [it], it is a complete gift for whatever he wishes [to do with it]; however, here, it is not in his power to transfer it to any person, for he gave it only so that his father would eat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:8:1.english: An incident to contradict? - For until now we have not seen [a case of] a defective gift.

Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:8:2.hebrew: ואם הוכיח סופו על תחילתו - פירוש: סוף דיבורו, כגון שסיים: "ואינם לפניך אלא כדי שיאכל פלוני"; אבל אמר ליה: "והם לפניך שיבא אביו" — מדעתו קאמר ליה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 48a:8:2.english: "And if his end proves [the nature of] his beginning" - Explanation: [This refers to] the end of his statement, such as where he concluded, "And they are before you only so that so-and-so may eat"; but [if] he said to him, "And they are before you so that his father may come," he is telling him [that it is] at his own discretion.
